pages.api:
# API reference

> Every field the cog reports, the store vector, the export endpoints, and the settings.

## stdout report (one per window)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED` or `SYNTHETIC` |
| `source` | string | `sysfs:<root>` or `simulated` |
| `sources` | object | booleans: `power`, `fan`, `thermal`, `load`, `mem` |
| `missing` | array | the names above that are false |
| `power_w`, `voltage_v`, `current_a` | number/null | window mean from the first INA2xx |
| `fan_rpm` | number/null | window mean of the fastest fan |
| `temp_max_c` | number/null | hottest zone reading in the window |
| `temp_by_group_c` | object | hottest per group: `cpu`, `gpu`, `npu`, `camera`, `ddr`, `other` (present groups only) |
| `load1`, `mem_available_mb` | number/null | |
| `power_monitors`, `fans`, `zones` | arrays | per-device detail from the last sample |
| `zones_unreadable` | int | zones skipped as unreadable or implausible |
| `vector_slots`, `vector` | arrays | the ingest vector and its slot names |
| `samples` | int | reads in the window |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 28)

Eight floats in physical units. A source that is absent is **-1** (no real reading is negative, and JSON cannot carry NaN).

| Slot | Name | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `power_w` | W |
| 1 | `voltage_v` | V |
| 2 | `current_a` | A |
| 3 | `temp_max_c` | C, hottest of all zones |
| 4 | `temp_npu_c` | C, hottest `nsp*` zone |
| 5 | `temp_cpu_c` | C, hottest `cpu*` zone |
| 6 | `fan_rpm` | RPM |
| 7 | `load1` | 1-minute load average |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8062`, continuous mode)

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /status` | the latest report |
| `GET /history` | `{"reports":[...]}`, the last 60 |
| `GET /guide` | this guide as JSON |
| `GET /healthz` | `{"ok":true}` |

## Settings (cog.toml / CLI)

| Setting | CLI | Default |
|---|---|---|
| interval | `--interval` | 5 s |
| window | `--window` | 2 s (`--once`) |
| sample_ms | `--sample-ms` | 1000 ms |
| sysfs_root | `--sysfs-root` | `/` |
| api bind | `--api-bind` | `127.0.0.1:8062` |
| simulate | `--simulate` | off |
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run the cog on the board, check it, and see where the numbers go.

## Check by hand first

```sh
for d in /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*; do echo "$d $(cat $d/name)"; done
for z in /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*; do echo "$z $(cat $z/type) $(cat $z/temp)"; done
```

An INA2xx shows up as `ina2xx`, `ina226`, `ina232` and so on. If the board has the part but no entry appears, the device-tree overlay or the kernel driver is not enabled; that is a board change, not a cog setting.

## Run it

```sh
cog-board-telemetry --once                   # 2 s window, one report
cog-board-telemetry --once --simulate        # synthetic values
cog-board-telemetry --interval 5             # continuous
cog-board-telemetry --once --sysfs-root DIR  # DIR must hold sys/ and proc/
```

## Outputs

| Output | Where |
|---|---|
| JSON report per window | stdout |
| 8-float vector, id 28 | `POST` to `$COGNITUM_INGEST_URL` when the node sets it (loopback `http://` only, else ignored with a warning), otherwise `127.0.0.1:80/api/v1/store/ingest`; only when `status` is `ok`. `$COGNITUM_COG_TOKEN`, if set, is sent as a bearer token |
| Export | `http://127.0.0.1:8062` (`/status`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`), continuous mode only |

`--simulate` never posts to the store.
pages.sources:
# What it reads

> Where each number comes from, and how the cog finds it without hard-coded device numbers.

Everything is found by name. hwmon and thermal zone numbers change between boards and between boots, so the cog scans `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*` and `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*` and decides from the contents.

| Number | Source | Unit conversion |
|---|---|---|
| `power_w` | hwmon whose `name` starts `ina2` (ina219, ina226, ina232, ina2xx): `power1_input` | microwatts to W |
| `voltage_v` | the same hwmon: `in1_input` (bus voltage) | millivolts to V |
| `current_a` | the same hwmon: `curr1_input` | milliamps to A |
| `fan_rpm` | any hwmon with `fanN_input` (for example emc2305, pwm-fan); the fastest fan | RPM as is |
| `temp_max_c` | every `thermal_zone*/temp` | millidegrees to degrees C |
| `temp_by_group_c` | the same zones, grouped by `type` | |
| `load1` | `/proc/loadavg`, first field | |
| `mem_available_mb` | `/proc/meminfo` `MemAvailable` | kB to MB |

If a driver exposes no `power1_input` but does give `in1_input` and `curr1_input`, the cog computes power as V times A and sets `power_derived` on that monitor.

## Thermal groups

A zone's `type` decides its group by prefix: `cpu*` is cpu, `gpu*` is gpu, `nsp*` is npu (the Qualcomm NPU on a Ventuno Q), `camss*` is camera, `ddr*` is ddr, anything else is other. Only groups that have a zone appear in `temp_by_group_c`.

A zone whose temperature cannot be read, or reads outside -50 to 150 C, is not counted as a temperature. It is counted in `zones_unreadable`.

## Reading `missing`

`missing` lists the sources this board does not have: any of `power`, `fan`, `thermal`, `load`, `mem`. The matching numbers are `null` in the report and `-1` in the vector.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Watch a board's power draw, fan and temperatures from the board itself, with no wiring.

This cog reads the monitors a Linux board already has and reports them once per window: input power, voltage and current from an INA2xx power monitor, fan RPM, the hottest thermal zone overall and per group (CPU, GPU, NPU, camera, DDR, other), the 1-minute load and free memory.

It opens no bus and needs no hardware change. If the kernel already shows the monitors under `/sys`, the cog can read them.

## The short path

1. **Check what the kernel exposes.** `ls /sys/class/hwmon /sys/class/thermal`. → see **What it reads**
2. **Install and run the cog.** `cog-board-telemetry --once` prints one report. → see **Set up**
3. **Read the `missing` list.** It names every source this board does not have. A Pi has no INA2xx or fan controller by default; that is normal, not a fault.
4. **Wire the vector to a consumer.** The 8 floats go to the store as id 28. → see **API**

You can test with no board at all: `--simulate` makes synthetic values marked `SYNTHETIC`, and `--sysfs-root DIR` reads a copy of a sysfs tree.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- It reports what the kernel reports. A driver that is not loaded is an absent source, not a zero.
- Temperatures are the maximum over the window; power, voltage, current, fan speed and load are the mean.
- Only the first INA2xx (lowest hwmon number) feeds the headline power. All of them are listed in `power_monitors`.
- Not yet verified on hardware: the layout is tested against fixture trees shaped like a Ventuno Q and a Raspberry Pi, not against a live board.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each status means and what to check.

**`no_source`.** None of an INA2xx power monitor, a fan controller or a thermal zone could be read.
- Run the commands in **Set up**. If they print nothing, the kernel exposes no monitors.
- Inside a container, `/sys` may be a stripped view. Mount the host's, or point `--sysfs-root` at a copy.
- A permissions error on `/sys/class/hwmon` shows as no source; run the cog as a user that can read it.

**`power` is in `missing` but the board has an INA2xx.** The driver is not bound. Check `dmesg | grep -i ina`.

**`zones_unreadable` is not zero.** Some thermal zones are disabled or report an impossible value. They are left out of every maximum on purpose.

**Fan RPM is 0.** That is what the controller reports. A stopped fan and a missing fan look different: a missing one is not listed at all.

**Nothing at `:8062`.** The export runs in continuous mode only (`--interval`), and binds loopback. Use `--api-bind` to change it.

**`status` is `simulate`.** `--simulate` is on. The values are synthetic and nothing is stored.

toml:
# Sensor guide for board-telemetry (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md). This cog reads the board it runs
# on, so there is no header pinout or wiring: the only diagram is the signal flow.

schema = 1
title = "Board Telemetry on a Linux board"
sensor = "On-board INA2xx power monitor, fan controller and thermal zones (sysfs)"
cog = "board-telemetry"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "sources", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
export = "setup"
sources = "sources"
power = "sources"
thermal = "sources"
fan = "sources"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "hwmon / thermal"
detail = "/sys/class/hwmon, /sys/class/thermal"

[[flow]]
name = "Find by name"
detail = "ina2xx, fanN_input, zone type"

[[flow]]
name = "Window"
detail = "mean rates, max temperatures"

[[flow]]
name = "board-telemetry cog"
detail = "report + 8-float vector"

[[flow]]
name = "Outputs"
detail = "stdout JSON, store vector, :8062 export"
